ideas.title: Gear it down: the winch that fills up
ideas.critique: The motor finally does work against a load the player picks, and that breaks the run of 'motor left alone at dusk' posts. The growing-radius drum, tension fed back through the gear ratio and tooth friction is real mechanics the cart reuses. Gear choice against load mass is a solid, if textbook, skill. The risk is that the film becomes one more fixed camera on the drum. The log slowing as the coil thickens has to be visible and has to come from the solver.

ideas.title: Tug of war with Pickles
ideas.critique: Mass from mesh volume and grip from mu times weight is general and the cart needs it. Heels skidding into furrows is a nerdy-funny gag carried by real numbers. The player's choice (which friend, which ground) is thin, and the payoff is mostly the friend's reaction, which caps the fun. A leaning pose that slides without real foot contact would turn into the sliding the human hates.

ideas.title: Crank it backwards: the drum lights a wire
ideas.critique: This is the strongest one. The player feels Lenz's law in Lumi's legs: back-EMF reused as a generator, braking torque on the rope, and a wire glowing from its I^2R heat balance. It is a whole road step, with an interaction that answers the player's effort. The glowing wire repeats 'Where I rushed it', so the new part has to be the run and the drag, not another close-up of a red filament.

ideas.title: The rope parts
ideas.critique: Breaking strength with cumulative wear and stored elastic energy snapping back is real failure physics, and a slow-motion whip clip is very shareable. On its own there is nothing to load the rope with yet except the existing log, so the player's decision only matters once heavier loads exist. A wear figure tuned so the rope breaks at the right moment would make it a rig.

ideas.title: The pots run down
ideas.critique: Faraday depletion that drives the colour and the internal resistance is exactly the road's 'cells that sag', and a cross-session resource economy gives the player a reason to come back. As a film, the pots slowly getting paler is the same six pots again with a different tint, which the judge will see as more of the same. The surprise is low.

ideas.title: A carbon brush from the campfire
ideas.critique: This is the third commutator-spark post in a row. A side-by-side night film of sparking brushes is the recipe of the last two posts with a black stick swapped in. The charring process and the material-driven contact resistance are real, but the contact numbers are typed per material and the brush trade-off is a single toggle.

ideas.title: Up the lookout tree
ideas.critique: The capstan friction and a pendulum basket with a real creature mass are sound, and lifting a friend is charming. Underneath it is the winch with the rope turned vertical, and the payoff (who shoots up, who dangles and waves) is the friends' reaction. The pose reacting to the swing is where it could look really good or fall into canned animation.

ideas.title: Lay the plank road
ideas.critique: The player builds something by hand and the soil physics judges it: sinkage per load and rolling resistance from contact rather than a table. That is the right direction and a real building mechanic. Carrying planks one at a time in a beak could turn into a chore, and a 'twentieth of the pull' that comes out of a tuned coefficient instead of the bearing model would make it a table in disguise.

ideas.title: Hear the stall coming
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Audio synthesised from the simulation's own changeover events and ripple is something the game never had, and hauling by ear is a lovely idea. It is infrastructure more than play, though: there is no goal beyond listening, and the browser streaming adds risk. The cart only gains a gauge you can hear.

ideas.title: A sail on the axle
ideas.critique: Blade-element momentum on the solved wind feeding a generator that replates the copper puts the 'yesterday's wind' loop into one machine, which is the big goal's core idea. It depends on the dynamo and depletion steps that do not exist yet, so trying it first risks a rotor that turns while a pot gets bluer, and nothing is shown to be causing it.
